name: NO Sales: Qualification Gates & Handoff
escalationContact: The weekly NO Sales sync, for a group decision
trigger: A prospect is deemed qualified by NO Sales, the lead is converted to an account and opportunity, and the opportunity moves to Meeting Scheduled in Salesforce.
purpose: NO Sales is the prospect's guide from first call to launch. If nobody hand-holds the prospect through each gate, reviews stall, prospects go cold, and launch dates slip. Scope: NO Sales, all verticals and markets.
doneWhen: Onboarding is kicked off with Ops and the coverage matrix is updated for the market.
timeToRun: 1 to 2 weeks from Ops handoff to cleared funnel

steps.title: Convert the lead and set the stage
steps.trigger: You have deemed the prospect qualified.
steps.work: Prompt Claude to run the lead conversion to account and opportunity, and move the opportunity to Meeting Scheduled. The qualification decision is yours; the conversion is automated. Verify the record yourself before moving on.
steps.doneWhen: The opportunity exists with the correct owner and the stage is Meeting Scheduled.

steps.title: Is the primary contact the right person?
steps.work: Verify the primary contact is the right person to run the gates with, usually the business owner or someone who can sign. It is a judgement call. Introducing a sales rep instead of the decision-maker has caused downstream delays and forced the whole gate cycle to repeat with the real owner, so check before the package goes to Ops.

steps.title: Pause and get the right contact on a call
steps.trigger: The primary contact turns out not to be the decision-maker.
steps.work: Pause the gates, get the right contact on a call, and restart the contact check with them.

steps.title: Package the prospect for Ops
steps.work: Assemble one package: call notes, the Salesforce record link, the fit assessment, the Sales Ranking, and the opportunity context covering client demand, market and primitives needed.
steps.doneWhen: The package is ready to send to the correct Ops owner in one message.

steps.title: Which Ops owner reviews this prospect?
steps.work: Pick the Ops reviewer by vertical: Event Ops goes to Yesenia or Joe, and Robotics, DPO or AV goes to Bryan or Michael B. The wrong Ops owner has happened before and new reps get this wrong most often, so when in doubt ask rather than guess.

steps.title: Ask TJ before sending anything
steps.trigger: The prospect does not map cleanly to a vertical.
steps.work: Ask TJ which Ops owner should review, and send nothing until he answers.
rules: Never guess the Ops owner; a misroute repeats the gate cycle.

steps.title: Schedule the facility visit
steps.trigger: The prospect is an AV or Robotics vertical.
steps.work: AV and Robotics prospects need a facility visit before the Ops ranking. Schedule it, brief the visitor, and capture the visit notes in Salesforce.

steps.title: Send the intro with the booking link
steps.work: Send the intro manually by email with the prospect and the Ops owner on the thread, including the Ops owner's booking link so the prospect schedules the call themselves. Chase if they have not booked within a few days.

steps.title: Ops gate
steps.trigger: The prospect has booked time with the Ops owner.
steps.work: Ops hosts the call, then logs notes and the Operations Ranking via Granola. An automation moves the opportunity stage and posts the Granola notes to Salesforce.

steps.title: Did the Ops ranking post?
steps.trigger: The Ops call has happened, or a week has passed without one.
steps.work: Check the Operations Ranking and Granola notes appear on the Salesforce record and the stage has advanced. If nothing posted, flag the automation rather than assuming Ops skipped the review.
steps.when: Chase if no ranking appears within the week after the call

steps.title: Chase the stalled Ops review
steps.trigger: The Ops review has sat without movement.
steps.work: Ping the reviewer directly. Never let a review sit silently; stalled reviews have killed prospects before. If it is still stuck, take it to the weekly sync. The NO evaluator call sweep shows when calls actually happened.
rules: Never let a review sit silently.

steps.title: Tom gate
steps.trigger: Ops has given the green light.
steps.work: Get Tom's call scheduled. Tom hosts it, then logs notes and Tom's Ranking via Granola. The same automation moves the opportunity stage and posts the notes to Salesforce.

steps.title: Did Tom's ranking post?
steps.work: Check Tom's Ranking and notes appear on the Salesforce record and the stage has advanced. If nothing posts, flag the automation before assuming Tom skipped it.

steps.title: Chase the stalled Tom review
steps.trigger: Tom's review has sat without movement.
steps.work: Ping Tom directly, and escalate to the weekly sync if it is still stuck.

steps.title: Do the three rankings agree?
steps.work: Salesforce calculates an aggregate score on the account, the average of the NO Sales, Ops and Tom rankings. Agreement clears the funnel; disagreement goes to the weekly sync.

steps.title: Decide as a group at the weekly sync
steps.work: Bring the conflict to the weekly in-person sync and decide together: advance, hold or kill. This is never a one-person or one-team call. Log the decision in Salesforce with the reason.
rules: Ranking conflicts are never resolved by one person or one team.

steps.title: Kick off onboarding
steps.trigger: The prospect has cleared the full funnel.
steps.work: Ops reaches out to the operator and coordinates onboarding and training. NO Sales confirms it happened rather than assuming. Triggering this automatically when the funnel clears is flagged as a future automation.
steps.doneWhen: Onboarding kickoff is scheduled and Ops has confirmed ownership of the relationship.

steps.title: Update the coverage matrix
steps.work: Future state. The coverage matrix does not exist yet. When live it will update itself: a launched operator's primitives move from Gap to Covered in that metro. Until then there is no action in this Automation.
